title: Trade as a Tool for the Green Transition: Indo-Pacific’s Emerging Green Economy Partnerships
gist: Excerpt of a TESS Forum piece by ASPI's Jane Mellsop arguing Indo-Pacific green economy partnerships bridge trade and environment goals by targeting behind-the-border barriers rather than market access, with FIT-P as an ideal vehicle.

insights.claim: New-generation Indo-Pacific green economy partnerships prioritize behind-the-border issues such as aligning standards, building supply chains and investment-led collaboration over the market access commitments of traditional trade agreements.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Watch standards harmonization and supply-chain provisions, not tariff cuts, as the channel for green trade integration.
insights.quote: The priority of these new partnerships is not on market access commitments that are found in traditional trade agreements.
insights.locator: The priority of these new partnerships

insights.claim: Countries in the Indo-Pacific are using international cooperation on the green economy to reconcile trade and environment goals, which have often been seen as conflicting because environmental measures can restrict trade or raise costs.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: Signals policy direction in which green-industry cooperation is framed as trade-enabling rather than trade-restricting.
insights.locator: Trade and environment goals have not always been easy bedfellows

insights.claim: The Future of Investment and Trade Partnership (FIT-P) is an ideal vehicle for expanding green economy cooperation because of its flexible design, broad membership and focus on contemporary trade issues.
insights.speaker: Asia Society Policy Institute
insights.so_what: FIT-P is an emerging framework to track for green supply-chain and investment rules in the region.
insights.locator: The fledgling Future of Investment and Trade Partnership
